goal: v0.3.0 Readiness Pro foundation: agent-agnostic profiles plus a --simulate harness that measures whether an AI agent picks the right operation with the right arguments for real user tasks, without calling the user's API.
gate: bash scripts/verify.sh (typecheck, tests, build, security audit). Unchanged from v0.2.
decision: 2026-09-24: focus on Readiness Pro (base.md top idea). The done-for-you service is parked on branch parked/services-offer, with drafts in outreach-parked/ (gitignored).
acceptanceCriteria: bash scripts/verify.sh passes after every task
--simulate never sends requests to the user's API: the simulated agent's tool calls are answered from the spec's own examples
The spec is only ever sent to a model endpoint the user configured, and the key comes only from an environment variable
Everything works without an LLM key; --simulate explains what it needs when none is set
securityRequirements: LLM calls live only under src/sim/. Adding that path to networkAllowedFiles in security/policy.json is a human decision (see H-101)
Refuse model IDs containing 'contributor' (Meta trains on that tier), and refuse any base URL that isn't HTTPS unless it's a local model
Spec contents, keys and model responses never appear in telemetry, because there is none; reports include only scores and the chosen calls

features.title: Agent profiles: --profile muse|mcp|openai-apps|claude|gemini
acceptanceCriteria: A profile is data (rule on/off and severity overrides plus a rationale), not code branches; muse stays the default so current output is unchanged
Profiles differ where the platforms actually differ, with a source cited per difference (for example OAuth-only is a fail for muse but a pass for claude and mcp)
--profile is available in the CLI, the config file (profile:) and the Action (profile input); the report header names the profile
Tests: the same fixture scores differently under muse and claude for the documented reasons; unknown profile names are rejected
bash scripts/verify.sh passes
features.notes: base.md: make the checker multi-target with the Muse ruleset as one plugin; this is the hedge if Meta ships its own validator.

features.title: SPEAK001: responses are short enough to speak (voice, glasses, Charm)
acceptanceCriteria: Static part: warn when list or detail response schemas have no short summary-like field (summary, title, name, label, description)
Live part (--probe): warn when a sampled response has no field under ~200 characters that could be read aloud
Thresholds labelled provisional, with the rationale citing Muse voice mode and glasses
Passing and failing cases in tests; good fixtures still pass; README catalog regenerated
bash scripts/verify.sh passes

features.title: Scenario files: muse-ready.tasks.yaml
acceptanceCriteria: Format: a list of scenarios, each with a user request in plain language, the expected operation(s) by operationId or method+path, and argument expectations (equals, contains, present, absent)
It can also mark a scenario as 'should refuse or ask' (for example destructive requests without confirmation)
It's validated with clear line-numbered errors; muse-ready can also generate a starter file from the spec (one read, one write, one destructive scenario)
Documented in README with an example for the Tasks fixture
bash scripts/verify.sh passes
features.notes: Deterministic grading lives here: the LLM proposes calls, and plain code checks them against these expectations.

features.title: Simulator core: OpenAI-compatible tool-calling client plus a mock API from spec examples
acceptanceCriteria: src/sim/ turns spec operations into tool definitions, runs each scenario through a configured model, and answers every tool call from the spec's examples (never from the network)
Model endpoint: any OpenAI-compatible base URL (Meta Model API, OpenRouter, OpenAI, a local model); key only from MUSE_READY_LLM_KEY; model and base URL from config or flags
Refuses '-contributor' model IDs and non-HTTPS remote endpoints (tests)
Scores per scenario: right operation, arguments meet expectations, no unexpected writes, turns used; repeated runs (default 3) to measure consistency
Tested against a deterministic fake model server in tests; no real LLM calls in CI
bash scripts/verify.sh passes (after H-101)
features.notes: Blocked on H-101 (policy change) and H-102 (model and key) for real use; the fake-server tests don't need either.

features.title: --simulate in the CLI, report and Action
acceptanceCriteria: --simulate [tasks file] runs the scenarios and adds a Simulation section: pass rate, per-scenario result, what the agent called and why it failed
The JSON report gains simulation: { model, runs, scenarios: [...] }; SARIF gets a finding per failed scenario pointing at the operation's description
Without a key it explains which env var and config it needs, and exits 2
The Action gains simulate and tasks-file inputs; the key comes from the workflow's env (a secret)
bash scripts/verify.sh passes

features.title: Human: allow network access from src/sim/ in security/policy.json
acceptanceCriteria: networkAllowedFiles includes src/sim/
features.notes: Approved by Oscar 2026-09-24; applied in a1dca19.

features.title: Human: choose the simulated-agent model and get a key
acceptanceCriteria: Model decided
Key available as MUSE_READY_LLM_KEY locally
features.skipReason: Needs an account and billing decision.
features.notes: base.md suggests Meta Model API muse-spark-1.3 (mirrors Muse, $20 free credits, OpenAI-compatible; never the -contributor tier), with a different model family as the judge because of the Spark 1.3 reward-hacking report.

features.title: Human: launch the free checker (Show HN, r/MuseAgent, X) and run it on ~20 public connector repos
acceptanceCriteria: Posts published
Results collected
features.skipReason: Outward-facing posts need the user's approval.
features.notes: base.md validation bar: 30+ stars and 5+ Action installs in two weeks, plus 3 people saying they'd pay for hosted simulation. This is the cheapest way to test Readiness Pro demand before building the hosted part.
